solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The Colt's legend as told by its creator?

indicators.note: as told signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a Colt is a gun, and a legend is a myth, so the gun's myth

explanation.surface: Someone asks who told the famous story of the Colt revolver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Colt's legend' spoken sounds like the word for the maker of firearms; 'as told' is the homophone signal and 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who makes firearms is the creator of a Colt revolver.

clue.text: Extremely gradual tingling leads to sudden hiccup

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two outer letters, of the word gradual

parts.note: a tingling on the skin is an itch

explanation.surface: A slow prickling sensation builds up until it brings on a hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: A glitch is a small sudden fault, a hiccup in the running of something.

clue.text: Little to do when modelling swimwear, say

definitions.meaning: having hardly anything happening or planned
wearing very few clothes, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both having few engagements and, literally, wearing scant clothing.

clue.text: Union given freedom that allows match-fixing!

parts.note: a union of two people is a marriage
licence is freedom to act as one pleases

explanation.surface: A trade union is set free and gets caught up in rigging matches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match-fixing' sounds like sporting corruption, but the match is a wedding and fixing is arranging it; 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The official permit is what lets a couple's wedding, a match, be arranged.

clue.text: Old hat-trick doesn't finish — or never starts

indicators.note: doesn't finish means the word trick loses its final letter
starts means only the opening letter of never is used

explanation.surface: A hat-trick is left incomplete, or is never even begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like a slang phrase for stale, but it is the definition of the three-cornered hat; 'hat-trick' must be split.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-cornered hat was a style of headwear worn in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Scrape off a scruffy beard

indicators.note: scruffy means untidy, so the letters of beard are messed up

explanation.surface: Someone shaves away an untidy beard.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape away a surface by rubbing or friction is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Start over, from the Piazza del Popolo, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to begin again from the very beginning

definitions.text: from the Piazza del Popolo, perhaps
definitions.meaning: returning from a famous Roman square, read literally

explanation.walkthrough: The Piazza del Popolo is a square in Rome, so heading back from it is literally going back to a square.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having to begin again after failing to make progress.

clue.text: Some trouble with sailors on deck

parts.note: a bit of trouble or fuss is ado
RN is the Royal Navy, crossword shorthand for sailors

explanation.surface: There is a bit of bother involving the sailors up on the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like part of a ship, but it is the verb meaning to decorate; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to decorate it, as in decking the halls.

clue.text: Festival starts to lose youth — a bitter blow for the UK

definitions.text: a bitter blow for the UK

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letters of the words lose and youth

explanation.surface: A festival that begins to lose its young people is a sad blow for Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bitter blow' reads as a setback but is a cold wind; British weather's coldest winds come from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind from the east, often bitterly cold in Britain, blows towards the UK.

clue.text: Kangaroo's startling cry gets me rattled at first

parts.note: boo is a cry made to startle someone

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of rattled

explanation.surface: A kangaroo gives a sudden shout and the narrator is shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kangaroo's' is Kangaroo is; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a large male kangaroo is called by this name.

clue.text: Bedouin terrorists' hiding place underground

indicators.note: hiding signals letters concealed within the words Bedouin terrorists

explanation.surface: Desert terrorists have a secret base below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter a body is to bury it, putting it in the ground.

clue.text: Press displeased with this award for bravery

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
cross means annoyed or displeased

explanation.surface: Journalists are unhappy about a medal for courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the news media but is the verb to iron; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The German military decoration was awarded for gallantry in battle.

clue.text: It could describe the end of tax, literally

definitions.text: It could describe the end of tax, literally

parts.words: It could describe the end of tax, literally
parts.note: the last letter of the word tax is X, which is shaped like a cross

explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' means look at the letters: the end of 'tax' is X, which has the shape of a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means shaped like a cross, as the letter X is.

clue.text: A suspicion can turn, for example

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: turn means the abbreviation for for example is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a suspicion can change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like the verb but is the container; 'turn' is the reversal signal on the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace, just a suspicion of a colour or quality.

clue.text: Japanese dictator's heartless weapon

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the weapon is removed

parts.note: a shotgun is a firearm, a weapon

explanation.surface: A Japanese ruler's gun is described as cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes out T, the middle letter of SHOTGUN; 'Japanese dictator's' is dictator is.
explanation.definitionFit: The hereditary military rulers of Japan held real power under the emperors.

clue.text: Victorian PM right to join American market

parts.note: to market goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century prime minister backs joining a US market.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord John Russell was Prime Minister twice in Queen Victoria's reign; 'to join' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord John Russell served as British Prime Minister in the Victorian era.

clue.text: Old company adapted Asian diet

indicators.note: adapted means changed, so the letters of Asian diet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historic firm changed its Asian diet.
explanation.walkthrough: The East India Company was the British trading company that ran much of India until 1858.
explanation.definitionFit: The East India Company was a historic British trading firm, dissolved in 1874.

clue.text: Unpunished — the reverse of what Wallace hoped to be

definitions.text: the reverse of what Wallace hoped to be
definitions.meaning: William Wallace fought to make the Scots free; swap the two words of that hope

explanation.walkthrough: William Wallace was the medieval Scottish patriot who fought for Scotland's freedom from England.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off without penalty is to escape entirely unpunished.

clue.text: Wicked things, maybe Roman

definitions.meaning: objects that have wicks, read literally
a Roman candle is a kind of firework

explanation.definitionFit: Wax lights have wicks, and a Roman one is a firework.

clue.text: The finest conductor? 40% agree!

definitions.meaning: this metal conducts electricity better than any other
the chemical symbol Ag is the first two of the five letters of agree

explanation.definitionFit: The metal is the best electrical conductor and has the chemical symbol Ag.

clue.text: Church protects what belongs to us, in a way

indicators.note: protects means the abbreviation for church surrounds the other piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
something that belongs to us is ours

explanation.surface: The church guards its own property in a certain fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a route or way taken, as a course of action.

clue.text: Business worry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commercial firm and a feeling of anxiety.

clue.text: Take off a commercial without endless fuss

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the advert goes around the other piece

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: making a scene is causing a fuss

explanation.surface: Someone removes a TV advert without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'endless' trims the final letter of the synonym for fuss before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft taking off rises into the air, which is to go up.

clue.text: Put on ice to keep something nice and fresh

indicators.note: to keep signals that the words Put on ice hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone chills food so that it stays fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is something refreshing and invigorating, or the fizzy mixer.

clue.text: New stars appear as East River rises

indicators.note: rises in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

explanation.surface: New stars come out as the river in the east swells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' reverses E plus AVON, the river through Stratford and Bath; 'appear as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Novae are stars that suddenly flare brightly, seeming to be newly born.

clue.text: Shy birds alight on fence

parts.note: to alight is to land
rails form a fence

explanation.surface: Timid birds settle on a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; a landrail is the corncrake, a secretive bird of meadows.
explanation.definitionFit: Landrails, or corncrakes, are secretive ground birds rarely seen in the open.

clue.text: Amorous interest shown by defective vision, apparently

definitions.meaning: a tendency to look at other possible partners
an eye that wanders, read literally as a faulty eye

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a habit of eyeing others romantically, read literally a wandering eye.

clue.text: Veteran soldier being shelled

indicators.note: being shelled means the outer letters of soldier are stripped off

explanation.surface: An old soldier comes under artillery fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old person or thing, a veteran.

clue.text: City of old beheaded saint

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the saint's name is cut off

parts.note: Peter is the apostle and saint

explanation.surface: A city in olden times had a saint executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; Exeter is the cathedral city of Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon in south-west England.

clue.text: Name Dr No created in custody

indicators.note: created means the letters of Name Dr No are made into something new

explanation.surface: Someone names the Bond villain Dr No as a creation.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr No is the villain of the first James Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner held awaiting trial is kept in custody.
